children.label: Basics
children: Anesthesia: reversible loss of consciousness and analgesia, with or without muscle relaxation (lecturer adds amnesia)
Phases: induction (mainly IV), maintenance (mainly inhalational), recovery
Gas (N2O in cylinders) or liquid via temperature-compensated vaporizer
Pathway: machine, vapor-oxygen mixture, lungs, blood, brain
Concentration example: 2 L O2 + 4 L N2O gives N2O 66%

children.label: MAC
children: Alveolar concentration at 1 atm preventing movement in 50% of patients at incision
Lower MAC means more potent; 1.2-1.3 MAC blocks movement in 95%
MAC: N2O 105%, enflurane 1.68%, isoflurane 1.16%, sevoflurane 2%, desflurane 6%, halothane 0.75%
Potency: halothane > isoflurane > enflurane > sevoflurane > desflurane > N2O
Higher MAC: hyperthermia, chronic alcohol use, acute amphetamines, hyperthyroidism
Lower MAC: old age, hypothermia, opioids, acute alcohol, pregnancy, hypothyroidism, clonidine
No effect: gender, duration of anesthesia, CO2 tension, hypertension, hyperkalemia

children.label: Uptake
children: To alveoli: higher delivered concentration, gas flow, minute ventilation
To brain: blood flow to brain, brain solubility, arteriovenous concentration difference
Agent moves along a partial pressure gradient and must be lipid soluble

children.label: Nitrous oxide
children: Only inhalational agent with analgesia; weak anesthetic used as adjuvant
Non-flammable, odorless, not metabolized, rapid diffusion
Diffusion hypoxia at end of surgery: give supplemental O2
Expands closed gas spaces: avoid in pneumothorax, bowel obstruction, middle ear surgery
Minimal CVS depression
Teratogenic with prolonged occupational exposure of staff; use scavenging
Second gas effect: fast N2O uptake speeds rise of a companion gas

children.label: Halothane
children: Most potent (MAC 0.75%), blood/gas coefficient 2.5, smooth induction
Bronchodilator, muscle relaxant, uterine relaxant
Arrhythmias: sensitizes myocardium to catecholamines
Poor analgesia, postoperative shivering, severe PONV
Hepatotoxicity: mild type 1 (25-30%), fulminant immune type 2 (1 in 6,000-35,000, mortality 30-80%)
Avoid repeat exposure within 3 months; ask about jaundice or fever after earlier use
Still used in Jordan because it is cheap

children.label: Enflurane and isoflurane
children: Enflurane: potent CV depressant, lowers seizure threshold (avoid in epilepsy), renal risk
Isoflurane: pungent, causes cough and breath-holding, used for maintenance not induction
Isoflurane: rapid recovery, cardiovascular stability, little hepatic or renal toxicity
Isoflurane: coronary vasodilation, coronary steal syndrome

children.label: Coronary steal syndrome
children: Vasodilator diverts blood from ischemic to normal myocardium
Narrowed arteries are already maximally dilated
Creates more ischemia in the diseased zone

children.label: Sevoflurane and desflurane
children: Sevoflurane: MAC 2%, sweet non-irritant, fastest induction, agent of choice for inhalational induction
Sevoflurane: compound A with soda lime (toxic to brain, liver, kidney), about 5% metabolized
Sevoflurane: postoperative agitation in children, does not sensitize myocardium much
Desflurane: MAC 6%, low potency, electrically heated vaporizer
Desflurane: poor induction agent, rapid recovery

children.label: Malignant hyperthermia
children: Triggers: all volatile agents (not N2O) and succinylcholine
Autosomal dominant, RYR1 mutation causes excess Ca2+ release from sarcoplasmic reticulum
Signs: muscle rigidity, tachycardia, rising CO2 production, fever (about 1 °C per 5 min)
Management: 100% O2, stop volatile agent
Cool the body and give fluids
IV dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg bolus then infusion over 72 h
Treat acidosis and hyperkalemia
